--- page 1 ---
Cover page: "Anticipatory Action Framework — Burkina Faso, Sécheresse" (drought). No figure.

--- page 2 ---
Résumé (summary) of the AA framework: pilot targets Boucle du Mouhoun, Centre-Nord, Sahel, Nord regions; potential to reach 800,000+ people. Three triggers (I, II, III) based on forecast/observed rainfall (IRI seasonal forecast, NOAA CMORPH SPI, UCSB GeoWRSI). Trigger I: March, JJA below-average rainfall risk. Trigger II: July, ASO below-average rainfall risk. Trigger III (Annex 2): Aug/Sep/Oct non-cumulative, SPI-1 < -1.5 or WRSI < 75. Narrative text, no figure.

--- page 3 ---
Continuation of activity list (protection, food security, malnutrition, WASH) and financing: CERF pre-arranged funding up to $15 million. Introduction section begins: "How anticipatory action works" diagram — 5-step flow: robust forecast & decision framework → pre-agreed actions → pre-arranged financing → anticipatory action → reduced crisis. No data values, just conceptual pipeline diagram.

--- page 4 ---
"Principe de base" (basic principles) narrative text listing 8 core principles (quality programming, multisectorial, protection centrality, accountability, localization, partnerships, cash, development co-benefits, learning). No figure.

--- page 5 ---
Text on drought exposure/climate zones plus two maps:
Map 1 "ZONES CLIMATIQUES DU BURKINA FASO (1981-2010)": Burkina Faso divided into 3 horizontal climate bands — Climat Sahélien (north, lightest, ~600mm), Climat Soudano-sahélien (center, ~600-900mm), Climat Soudanien (south, darkest, 900+mm); shows provinces/cities (Dori, Ouahigouya, Kaya, Ouagadougou, Bobo-Dioulasso, etc.) and neighboring countries (Mali, Niger, Ghana, Togo, Benin, Côte d'Ivoire). Source: Direction Générale de la Météorologie.
Map 2 "Drought risk" (WFP 1981-2015): choropleth of Burkina Faso admin regions — High risk (red) concentrated in the north (Sahel region), Medium (orange) covering central band, Low (yellow/cream) in south/southwest.

--- page 6 ---
Four small choropleth maps of Burkina Faso admin regions (2x2 grid):
1. "Multidimensional poverty index" (Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative, 2020): scale 0.1–0.7, highest (0.6-0.7, dark magenta) in north/center-north, lowest in southwest.
2. "Number of IDPs" (OCHA, 2020): scale 0–500,000; highest concentration (300,000-500,000, dark red) in north/Sahel-Centre-Nord area; rest of country near 0.
3. "Population" (OCHA, 2019): scale 500,000–3,000,000; highest population (2.5-3M) in Centre region (around Ouagadougou).
4. "Population IPC 3+" (FSNWG, 2020, averaged across year): scale 0–1,200,000; highest (1,000,000-1,200,000, dark teal) in Sahel/Centre-Nord provinces.
Text: drought cumulatively affected 12.4M people 1969-2014; CH Oct-Dec 2021 showed 5/16 provinces in Phase 3 (crisis), 6 in Phase 2.

--- page 7 ---
Two side-by-side CH (Cadre Harmonisé) food insecurity maps of Burkina Faso:
Left: "Oct-Dec 2021" — Phase classification by province; Phase 3 (Crise, orange) in north/Sahel provinces (e.g., Séno, Oudalan), Phase 2 (Sous pression, yellow) scattered north/center, Phase 1 (green) covers south/west, one small Phase 4 (Urgence, dark red) area near Séno/Oudalan.
Right: "Juin-Juillet-Août 2022" projection — worse: large dark red Phase 4 (Urgence) zone in far north (Oudalan, Séno), more provinces in Phase 3 (orange), fewer in Phase 1.
Below: map "Number of humanitarian activities" (OCHA 2021): scale 0–10,000, highest concentration (8,000-10,000, dark green) in Centre-Nord/Sahel provinces.
Adjacent map: Burkina Faso regions with orange circles sized by "Nombre de personnes dans le besoin" (people in need), largest circles over Sahel and Centre-Nord regions, blue shading indicating severity, scale bar 100km.

Seasonal calendar chart (source: FEWSNET) spanning May–April: shows Préparation des sols, Saison des pluies (rainy season roughly June-Oct), Récolte principale (main harvest Oct-Dec), Récolte de contre-saison, Période de soudure (lean season, red bar ~June-Sept), Orpaillage (gold mining) periods, Migration du bétail (livestock migration) bars.

--- page 9 ---
Large Gantt-style "Calendrier de la crise sécheresse" (drought crisis calendar) table spanning 2 years x 12 months (J-D), rows: Climat, Risque (Sécheresse), Impact Humanitaire, and impact categories (Agricole cultures pluviales/fourragères, Agricole cultures maraîchères) each shaded across specific months showing progression of impact — colors intensify (light to dark) June through Oct/Nov indicating escalating humanitarian consequence.

--- page 10 ---
Continuation of crisis calendar table: rows for Elevage, Alimentaire, Nutrition, WASH, Protection — each shows color bands (light→dark) spanning different month ranges (roughly June–Dec and again the following June-Nov), illustrating cascading/lagged sectoral impacts of drought. Legend: lighter = lower need, darker = higher need.
Section "3. Prévision et déclencheur" begins: describes trigger overview, Trigger I/II based on IRI seasonal forecast, Trigger III based on observational SPI/WRSI thresholds (SPI-1<-1.5 or WRSI<75 over ≥30% of zone). Narrative text, no chart.

--- page 11 ---
Narrative text on forecasts (IRI seasonal forecast issued mid-March and mid-July), trigger thresholds: ≥40% probability below-average rain AND that probability ≥5pts higher than above-average probability; SPI-1<-1.5 or WRSI<75 over ≥30% of zone; activation requires ≥10% of the 4 target regions meeting criteria. Also describes activation protocol steps (CHD → OCHA HoO → CH/CR → EHP/agencies → CERF). No figure.

Narrative text: continued monitoring/activation protocol; Section "4. Plan de l'Action Anticipatoire" — selection criteria (anticipatory nature, deliverability in window, operational capacity, no-regret approach) and intervention properties (protection, food security/livelihoods FAO/WFP, malnutrition UNICEF, WASH UNICEF). No figure.

Table "Sommaire" (summary) of Results/Sector/Agency/Proposed activities: Protection (UNFPA, UNHCR, UNICEF) — dignity kits, GBV/PSEA sensitization, case management; Sécurité alimentaire & Moyens d'existence (FAO, WFP) — rainfed/livestock/maraîchage support, cash for work, conditional/unconditional transfers; Nutrition (UNICEF) — malnutrition referral, IYCF, micronutrient supplementation; WASH (UNICEF) — water point rehab, hygiene kits.

--- page 31 ---
"Annexe 2 – Mise à jour de juillet 2023" narrative: context update — March 2023 CH showed 2 Sahel provinces in Phase 4, 9/22 provinces in Phase 3, 16 in Phase 2; by June 2023 projected 15 provinces in crisis (Ph3+), 3.35M people needing immediate assistance (~15% of population), concentrated in Sahel (21%), Centre-Nord (16%), Est (16%), Nord (14%), Boucle de Mouhoun (12%). Introduces two new observational triggers: SPI (Standard Precipitation Index) and WRSI (Water Requirement Satisfaction Index), monitored July-Sept for a new 9-month activation window. Narrative text, no chart.

--- page 32 ---
Table "Mois du calendrier / Indicateur / Période observée / Moment du calcul": Juillet (SPI-1: 2-31 July; WRSI: start of season to 3rd decade of July) calculated 3 August; Août similarly calculated 3 September; Septembre calculated 3 October.
Diagram: timeline Jan-Nov showing "Saison des pluies" bracket (Jul-Oct) with 5 "Moment potentiel d'activation" boxes: March (purple, based on seasonal forecasts), July (purple), and Aug/Sep/Oct (green, based on season progression/observational). Box states trigger condition: SPI<-1.5 OR WRSI<75 over ≥30% of zone (~28.5% probability of activation, i.e., 1 year in 3.5).

Below: list of 4 priority action areas (protection, food security/livelihoods, malnutrition, water access).

--- page 36 ---
Text "Financement pré-accordé" (update): CERF funds only disbursed once observational trigger (Annex 2) is activated, and only if no March/July trigger activation already occurred.
Table "Scénarios possibles": 5 activation scenarios with budgets — Scénario 1 (March+July trigger): Protection/FS/WASH/Nutrition, $14.5M; Scénario 2 (March only): Protection/FS/WASH, $9M; Scénario 3 (July only): FS/Nutrition, $5.5M; Scénario 4 (July + Aug/Sep/Oct): all 4 sectors, $15M; Scénario 5 (Aug/Sep/Oct only): all 4 sectors, $9.5M. Grouped as "Scénarios initiales" (1-3) vs "Scénarios additionnels" (4-5). Note: March trigger activation precludes later Aug/Sep/Oct observational activation.
